why_how.text: Slow and stay alert near stopped fire, police, ambulance, disaster-support, highway-maintenance or recovery vehicles with flashing emergency lights.
The move-over rule requires a cautious reasonable safe speed when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
On a highway with at least four lanes including two in your direction, safely change to a lane not beside the stopped emergency vehicle.
The safe move-over direction may be right or left, and if a lane change is impossible the driver must still slow and proceed cautiously.
Be ready to stop when passing an emergency vehicle and dim high beams at night.
If requesting police assistance, stop in front of the cruiser rather than behind it.
Do not approach an officer handling another stopped driver; wait beside your own vehicle on the shoulder until the officer finishes.
Driving by or parking within eight hundred feet of a fire is prohibited.
Do not drive across an unprotected fire hose unless a firefighter or public-safety official directs you to do so.

During a stop, select Park in an automatic or neutral with the parking brake in a manual vehicle, and turn off the engine and radio.
The driver and passengers should remain inside until the officer instructs otherwise.
If directed out, stay safely away from traffic and keep hands visible.
At night during a police stop, leave headlights on and turn on the interior overhead light.
Lower the window as the officer approaches.
An officer not in uniform will show credentials, or the driver may ask to see them.
Wait for a request before reaching for license or registration and hand the documents over outside a wallet or holder.
Keep license and registration handy while driving; a first failure to produce either document carries a thirty-five-dollar fine.
Without the documents, the officer may request the driver’s name and address and the owner’s name and address when different.
Failure to comply with the identity request or giving a false name or address can bring a one-hundred-dollar fine, and refusal may lead to arrest and criminal charges.
A Massachusetts registration identifies the insurer and explains that Massachusetts does not issue an insurance card, while other jurisdictions may request insurance proof under their laws.
Keep both the driver’s and passengers’ hands plainly visible.
Give the officer full attention without using a cell phone during the stop.
Avoid sudden movements or reaching into hidden areas, and make sure passengers avoid those movements too.
Remain in the vehicle when the officer goes back to the cruiser.
